title: Check yourself: Reading usage, counting tokens before sending, and modelling cost

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A response reports 120 `input_tokens`, 4,000 `cache_creation_input_tokens` and 340 `output_tokens`. A team adds them up as 460 tokens in and out. What does the page say they missed?

options.text: The output tokens are priced from the cache multiplier
options.says: Ruled out because output tokens are "Tokens generated, thinking included" and the table prices them at the output price, while the cache multipliers apply to input.

options.text: The cache write has its own price above the base input price
options.says: The page prices a 5-minute cache write at "1.25 times input", so 4,000 written tokens are not ordinary input.

options.text: The count in `input_tokens` already includes the written tokens
options.says: Ruled out because `input_tokens` is "Input tokens that were not read from or written to a cache".

options.text: The batch discount applies to cache writes before anything else
options.says: Ruled out because the batch discount is "50 percent on input and output" and halves the sum, and it is not an ordering of charges.

questions.stem: Before sending a long prompt, an application wants to know whether it fits a budget. Which tool does the page back, and with what caveat?

options.text: The pricing page, whose figures give the token count of any prompt
options.says: Ruled out because the pricing page gives prices per million tokens, while the endpoint "takes the same structured input as a Messages request" and counts it.

options.text: A trial request with a tiny `max_tokens`, whose usage is exact and free of charge
options.says: Ruled out because a trial request is a billed Messages call (the page calls counting "free to use"), while the page offers counting as a separate call with "separate and independent rate limits".

options.text: The `input_tokens` of the previous response, which always predicts the next one
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "to decide before paying" with counting on the new prompt, and an earlier response predicts nothing about it.

options.text: The token counting endpoint, whose figure is an estimate and is free to request
options.says: The page says "The token count is an estimate" and "Token counting is free to use but subject to requests per minute rate limits based on your usage tier."

questions.stem: A router must pick between two models whose costs for a cache-heavy request are equal. What does the practice's rule do?

options.text: It takes the first model in the catalog, since order is the only signal left
options.says: Ruled out because a router that breaks ties by list order gives "an answer that depends on how the catalog was written".

options.text: It takes the lower tier, so the answer does not depend on the catalog
options.says: The practice's rule is "A cost tie goes to the lower tier", and the order of the catalog never matters.

options.text: It takes the larger window, since room is worth keeping in reserve
options.says: Ruled out because the rule is "A cost tie goes to the lower tier" and never ranks windows once the limits are met.

options.text: It takes the higher tier, since quality is worth the extra spend
options.says: Ruled out because the statement says "goes to the lower tier".
